Forensic Team & Evidence Preservation

The forensic team, evidence types and preservation, and nursing responsibilities in medico-legal investigation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List the members of the forensic team
  • Describe evidence types and preservation
  • Explain the nursing role in the forensic team
  • Follow medico-legal investigation practice

In simple words

Forensic investigation is teamwork. The nurse is a key member who supplies victim care, first-hand observations and preserved evidence.

The forensic team

Member Role
Doctor (forensic pathologist) Examines, certifies, performs postmortem
Nurse First contact, care, observation, evidence support, documentation
Police Investigation, custody of accused, legal orders
Investigating officer Leads case investigation and evidence collection
Forensic laboratory Analyses samples and prepares reports
Social worker / counselor Victim support and rehabilitation
Lawyer / public prosecutor Legal proceedings

Types of evidence

Type Example Preservation
Physical Weapons, broken glass, bullets Dry, sealed, labelled, never cleaned
Biological Blood, hair, semen, tissue Cool and dry, sealed, avoid contamination
Chemical Poison, drugs, alcohol Sealed bottle, refrigerated if needed
Documentation Records, prescriptions, notes Photograph and safe custody

Do’s and don’ts of evidence handling

Do: wear gloves, change gloves between samples, label after sealing, keep wet samples cool, record every step, hand over with signature. Don’t: clean or dry bloody clothes, use the same container for different samples, leave samples unattended, label before collection, hand over without signatures.

Scene of crime

  • Nothing is touched or moved until authorised
  • Record what is found, where and by whom
  • Photographs and sketches are made before removal
  • Samples are removed with proper documentation

🔴 Nursing observation is evidence

The nurse who sees position of the body, spillage, smell, burns pattern or defensive injuries provides the first and often the strongest observation. Record it immediately and factually.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Forensic team: doctor, nurse, police, laboratory, social worker, lawyer.
  2. Evidence types: physical, biological, chemical and documentary.
  3. Preserve evidence dry, sealed, labelled, cool and secure.
  4. Never clean or dry evidence bearing garments.
  5. Every transfer of evidence is signed and timed.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Use separate gloves and containers for each sample.
  2. Wet samples must be dried and packed in paper, not plastic.
  3. Sealed containers with initials and date identify ownership.
  4. Refer complaints of custodial violence to proper authorities.
  5. Support victims and families throughout the process.

📌 Memory trick

Evidence handling: S-L-C-S — Seal, Label, Cool, Sign.

60-second revision

  • Forensic team members and their roles.
  • Evidence types: physical, biological, chemical, documentary.
  • Preserve: seal, label, cool, sign; never clean.
  • Record scene findings immediately and factually.
  • Handover is signed and timed.

Test yourself

Which is biological evidence?

Answer: B. Blood, hair, semen and tissue are biological evidence analysed for DNA and other markers.

Wet blood-stained clothes should be:

Answer: B. Wet evidence is dried and packed in paper bags to prevent mould and contamination.

At the scene of crime, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Nothing is moved or cleaned; the scene is observed, recorded and photographed.

Two samples from one case should:

Answer: B. Separate, clearly labelled containers prevent cross-contamination.

'Sign' in evidence handling means:

Answer: B. Each transfer is signed with date and time so the chain of custody remains unbroken.
